what_its_for: Tobramycin is an antibiotic used to fight certain bacterial infections. It is most commonly used to treat lung infections caused by a germ called Pseudomonas aeruginosa in people with cystic fibrosis. The eye drop form is used to treat bacterial eye infections. It works by stopping bacteria from growing and multiplying.
how_to_take: Tobramycin comes in different forms depending on your condition. The inhaled liquid form (nebulizer solution) is breathed in through a nebulizer machine — do not swallow it. The inhaled capsule form (Podhaler) is used with a special inhaler device — never swallow the capsules. The eye drop form is placed directly into the affected eye. Always wash your hands before using any form of this medication. Follow the instructions your doctor or pharmacist gave you for your specific form carefully.
dosing: For inhaled tobramycin (nebulizer or Podhaler): The usual dose for cystic fibrosis patients is taken twice a day, about 12 hours apart, for 28 days. Then you take 28 days off the medication. This on-and-off cycle then repeats. For eye drops: The usual dose is 1 to 2 drops in the affected eye every 4 to 6 hours, or as directed by your doctor. For severe infections, your doctor may start you on a higher frequency. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if there are at least 6 hours before your next scheduled dose. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are on the 28-day on/off cycle and miss several days, contact your doctor for guidance.
storage: Inhaled solution (nebulizer): Store unopened pouches in the refrigerator (36°F to 46°F / 2°C to 8°C). Once opened, you may store the pouches at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C) for up to 28 days. Keep them away from heat and light. Podhaler capsules: Store at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C). Always keep the capsules in the blister pack until right before use. Eye drops: Store at room temperature (59°F to 77°F / 15°C to 25°C). Keep all forms away from moisture and out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid skipping doses or stopping this medication early, even if you feel better — finishing your full course helps make sure the infection is fully treated. For the inhaled form, avoid using it near an open flame or while smoking. For eye drops, avoid touching the tip of the dropper to your eye, fingers, or any surface to prevent contamination. Avoid wearing contact lenses while using the eye drop form unless your doctor says it is okay. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially other antibiotics, diuretics (water pills), or medications that may affect your kidneys or hearing.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: ringing or buzzing in your ears, hearing loss, or difficulty hearing; dizziness or spinning sensation; decreased urination or swelling in your legs, which could be signs of kidney problems; wheezing, chest tightness, or trouble breathing after inhaling the medication; severe coughing or coughing up blood; eye redness, increased pain, swelling, or vision changes (with eye drops); signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your symptoms are not improving or are getting worse.
when_it_works: For lung infections with the inhaled form, you may start to notice improvement in your breathing within the first few weeks of treatment, but the full benefit is usually seen after completing the 28-day treatment cycle. For eye infections, improvement is typically noticed within 2 to 3 days of starting the eye drops. Always complete the full prescribed course of treatment even if you feel better sooner.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Tobramycin may cause harm to an unborn baby if absorbed into the bloodstream. Use only if your doctor decides the benefit outweighs the risk. Kidney problems: Tobramycin can affect the kidneys, so your doctor may need to monitor your kidney function more closely or adjust your dose if you have kidney disease. Hearing problems: If you already have hearing difficulties, tell your doctor before starting this medication, as tobramycin can rarely affect hearing. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of tobramycin on the kidneys and hearing, so extra monitoring may be needed. Children: Inhaled tobramycin is approved for use in children with cystic fibrosis aged 6 years and older. Follow your child's doctor's instructions carefully.
